reviews_data.review_text:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but our experience at Desert Rose in Doha was disappointing from start to finish. We came here for dinner on an evening right before the Formula 1 race weekend, expecting the restaurant to be prepared for guests—especially since it wasn’t even particularly busy. Unfortunately, everything about the visit fell short.

Food:
We ordered a cold mezze and a mixed grill, both of which were extremely underwhelming. The food arrived tasteless, tepid, and lacking any freshness. The mezze felt tired and uninspired, and the mixed grill came out lukewarm with no seasoning to redeem it. For the price, the quality was shockingly poor.

Service:
The service was slow, confused, and inattentive. Despite the restaurant being far from full, we were left waiting at every stage—from ordering, to receiving our food, to simply trying to get our bill. Staff seemed disorganized and uncertain, making the whole experience feel chaotic and unprofessional.

Value for Money:
For what we got, the value was nothing short of terrible. We paid 435 QR (about £95 GBP) for two disappointing dishes and lackluster service. At that price point, you expect quality, flavor, and at least a basic level of attentiveness—none of which we received.

Overall:
This was a poor dining experience from beginning to end. Nothing about our visit suggested the restaurant cares about quality, service, or guest satisfaction. With so many genuinely excellent options in Doha, I can’t recommend spending your time or money at Desert Rose.
I came for coffee and desserts and I got a 40 QAR kunafa made with Philadelphia cheese. Taste was really unacceptable. It remained untouched but I was still charged for it. Not coming back.

Отдельно удивил уровень подготовки персонала. Официант не смог ответить на простой вопрос о составе салата «Оливье» и не знал, входят ли в него яйца. Для ресторана, представляющего славянскую кухню, это выглядит крайне непрофессионально.

Считаю, что заведению стоит серьёзно пересмотреть как качество блюд, так и подготовку сотрудников. Представлять украинскую и славянскую кухню на таком уровне — скорее антиреклама, чем повод для гордости

Visited Çöl Gülü Restaurant in Doha’s historic center on a Friday morning. Due to Friday hours, there was no breakfast service, and lunch follows after 12:30 Since I don’t love heavy meals early in the day, I went simple with a small cheese pide and Turkish tea.

The place has a nostalgic, traditional atmosphere, though it could use a bit of maintenance. The pide was hot and tasty, and the tea was properly brewed, which always earns points. The menu looks quite rich, especially the bakery items, so I imagine those are worth trying on a fuller visit.
